A spiking model emits $\bar{r}\times\mathrm{FLOPs}$ synaptic events on each of its $T=8$ integration steps, so its count is $\mathrm{SOP}_{spiking}=T\times\bar{r}\times\mathrm{FLOPs}_{dense}$ with the measured firing rate $\bar{r}$; a dense baseline performs a single forward pass and carries no $T$ factor. Including $T$ is required for the comparison to be like-for-like, and it reduces the advantage over the dense reference from a naive $1-\bar{r}\,e_{SOP}/e_{FLOP}$ to the values reported here. FLOPs are analytic per-architecture counts. Reductions are relative to the capacity- and backbone-matched dense Proto-GIN at the same shot. The 5-shot spiking cells are priced at the measured 5-shot firing rate $\bar{r}$ printed in their row label; a dense per-graph forward pass carries no firing-rate or $T$ factor, so its 1-shot and 5-shot entries coincide. Per-operation constants are literature values, not device measurements; the independent event-count re-derivation is detailed in Section~\ref{sec:energy}.}
